body:
Opening `/network/?code=003002&solve=true` previously cut the purple link before its middle despite both configured middle cuts being zero. Automatic spacing now preserves the configured cuts by default. The editor and solver both default their automatic middle-cut allowance to zero; a positive explicit allowance still enables the existing cut-adjustment feature. The field explains this in English and Russian.

Fixes #35.

## Reproduction and tests

- Open the reported URL with automatic spacing enabled. Before the fix, the link paths have subpath counts `[1, 2, 1]`; after the fix all are continuous: `[1, 1, 1]`.
- Six new unit/DOM regressions were run before implementation and failed, then passed after the fix. They cover the editor and direct solver, global/per-link cuts and zero overrides, explicit automatic-cut opt-in, and Apply/share round trips.
- `npm run test:network:issue35` checks native SVG continuity and twelve raster pixels approaching the purple middle, zero-cut settings, exact Apply/share/reload output, an actual SVG download, and intentional cut behavior. It is included in the existing Chromium/Firefox/WebKit CI matrix.

Validation passes:

- All 871 unit/DOM tests in 64 files, including the six new regressions.
- New native regression in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit locally; final Playwright MCP verification of the exact reported URL.
- Production build and all 120 CV PDFs with page-count, text-layer and reading-order checks.
- ESLint, Prettier, file limits, secret scan, Python/Ruff, shellcheck and dependency audit.
- [Final-head CI](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40932135113) passes on commit `18e013ffc461ea058b12be39871f4d3bd0d47e97`, including every existing browser suite in Chromium, Firefox and macOS WebKit, CodeQL and the final pipeline gate. The run completed successfully on 2026-10-29 at 18:47:44 UTC; deployment is intentionally skipped for pull requests.

Additional local compatibility runs pass all six suites in Chromium and Firefox and three in Linux WebKit. Linux WebKit times out on two gallery hovers and one background-settings keyboard operation; those exact suites pass in macOS CI. The logs and the connection to the documented Linux WebKit r2370 rendering limitation are recorded in the case study. No assertions or timeouts were weakened.

[Investigation, requirement map and saved reproduction logs](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-35-0a1c09fbb17e/docs/case-studies/issue-35/README.md).

body:
Repository cards now show per-language code, comment and blank-line counts at measured public revisions. The home page adds personal Git-attributed source totals, including outside projects, and the actual GitHub daily graph with shared anonymized private activity. The discipline slogan appears only for a fresh, uninterrupted recent contribution habit.

The change also refreshes the public profile, repository/organization catalog, registries, Stack Overflow, Habr and social archive; labels snapshot numbers with (*) and footer dates; prefers supported social embeds with a readable archive and retry; upgrades outdated npm and CI tooling dependencies; and adds the current associative application entry. Existing annual charts, editor behavior and CV variants are retained.

The completed source census covers 1,737 public repositories with zero errors, including whole-repository counts for all 527 displayed projects. It credits 13,224,518 surviving nonblank Git-attributed lines across 95 cloc language categories; 4,461,732 of those lines are credited in 260 repositories outside the personal and organization accounts. The independent durable-cache verification passes for every measurement and language total.

The complete public ecosystem audit covers 1,912 repositories. Three manifest/source-backed guide omissions were reported in [Formal AI issue 1455](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1455).

Fixes #33.

## Scope and evidence

Source statistics use public default branches only. Personal figures count surviving nonblank programming/markup lines, including comments, attributed to verified account identities; they exclude prose/data, saved patches and dependency/build directories, and deduplicate shared Git history. Git attribution includes tool-assisted work and cannot establish manual typing or count deleted work. Private code and repository metadata are excluded; only the calendar includes the explicitly requested anonymized private aggregates.

The public calendar mirror currently disagrees with GitHub on completed days, so the site retains the exact dated first-party graph. Compatible live responses can replace it. VK records without a provider export hash and the configured personal Telegram account retain their supported archive/original-link behavior. GitHub Packages exposes rounded public download figures because the token lacks package-read permission; the collected registry coverage limits remain explicit.

[Case study, requirement inventory and alternatives](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-33-bcf9257c5489/docs/case-studies/issue-33/README.md) · [Collection commands, reproductions and validation](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-33-bcf9257c5489/docs/case-studies/issue-33/VALIDATION.md)

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before this change, `/#activity` contains annual charts but no daily calendar or personal source totals; `/repositories/?q=links-notation#all` has no per-language line counts; and `/blog/?lang=en&network=x` opens archived text before the original widget. The feature regressions fail on that implementation, with their output preserved in the case study.

The new unit/DOM and browser checks cover these flows, exact calendar dates/counts/levels and both palettes, compatible/conflicting/offline refreshes, slogan expiry, source coverage and sum consistency, mobile layouts and social archive/retry. Twelve finite local Git/cloc fixtures verify public-only attribution, shared-history deduplication and checkpoint recovery. The independent checkpoint verifier checks the complete source census against its durable original-line identities.

## Validation

Final commit `c779998982ec40c4629cb6faf53db616f332dc21` passed [CI run 40778088944](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40778088944), created at 22:11:57 UTC and completed at 22:22:52 UTC on 2026-10-28. All 13 required jobs passed, including Chromium, Firefox, native macOS WebKit, unit/build/PDF verification, tooling, documentation, security analyses and the pipeline gate. Deployment was correctly skipped for the pull request. The preceding [complete implementation run](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40776059468) also passed.

Final review matched all 177 PR file paths and blob hashes to the local commit. Latest `main` (`bb88ed9437a1b26cb43b7fc1436fe885080c113d`) is an ancestor, the working tree is clean, and the PR is ready for review and left unmerged.

- 865 unit/DOM tests in 62 files; twelve finite Git/cloc collector fixtures and independent verification of the complete attribution database.
- Production build and all 120 CV PDF variants, including page limits and searchable text.
- Real-browser indicator regression with the complete dataset, both themes, English/Russian mobile layouts, expanded attribution evidence and social archive/retry. All seven existing Chromium editor browser scripts also pass, including the finite 1,215-card gallery probe.
- ESLint, Prettier, source-size and secret checks; Python syntax, Ruff, ShellCheck, 42 workflow-policy tests, documentation and regular/pedantic zizmor audits.
- No outdated npm dependencies and zero npm audit vulnerabilities.

The main Pages run failed at `CreateArtifact: ENOTFOUND` after its browser assertions passed. Evidence and Pages uploads now share the official artifact SDK with three bounded attempts for transient transport/429/5xx failures. Permanent failures, empty evidence and exhausted retries fail. A partial-success retry reconciles the existing artifact before replacement, and Pages retains the official tar-in-ZIP format.

The complete audit also found CI false greens and platform-only warnings. The PR:

- Fixes native ESM imports throughout the settings configuration graph, extracts the oversized collector helper, and avoids unsupported jsdom canvas noise while retaining real-browser coverage.
- Adds complete terminal job coverage, fresh-merge and relevant-change checks, Python/Ruff/ShellCheck, actionlint, zizmor, full CodeQL scans in all three languages, documentation checks, scheduled lock audits and early Pages preflight. Read jobs cancel independently; deployments serialize. Deploy verification checks the commit, actual JavaScript and PDF signature.
- Resolves the macOS npm advisory through a reviewed approval for **fsevents@2.3.3** only. The all-platform lockfile test requires a new review for another version. A narrow, tested glob override removes the SDK's deprecated transitive dependency warning.
- Fixes all ten full-scan CodeQL findings: two regex hangs, regex HTML extraction/text stripping, incomplete package-name encoding, inline script JSON boundaries, both hostname matchers and dynamic test-label escaping. HTML parsing uses the already locked parse5; all 63 archived post bodies retain their text apart from documented browser-equivalent NUL normalization. Existing data and media are unchanged.
- Makes each security job inspect its actual SARIF results after analysis. The prior workflow passed while the separate CodeQL check failed; findings, missing/malformed reports and unsuccessful tool invocations now fail the workflow as well. All default queries, maintained-source coverage and the independent check remain enabled. Full scans also avoid CodeQL's 300-file compare limit for this evidence-heavy PR.

All seven browser suites, three engines, the exact 4,131-card gallery case, compositor captures and all 120 PDF checks remain enabled. This private website has no package/container publishing target; Pages remains its release mechanism. Development requires Node 24, matching CI and the artifact SDK. Source archives without Git metadata still build.

Validation: **833 tests in 55 suites pass locally**, plus production build, lint/format/secret/file limits, Python/Ruff/ShellCheck, pinned actionlint, both zizmor modes and a zero-vulnerability committed-lock audit. The independent CodeQL check passes with zero open PR-merge alerts. Complete final raw logs contain no warnings or errors; all annotations are informational notices. The working tree is clean and current main is an ancestor.**

The [collected investigation](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/issue-31-ec772c60ce96/dev/log/issues/31/pulls/32) includes every requirement and solution plan, all 17 guide principles, all **603 template paths** classified/hashed, original template snapshots, complete CI logs, before/after regressions, [verification](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-31-ec772c60ce96/dev/log/issues/31/pulls/32/VERIFICATION.md), and the [ten-alert security inventory](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-31-ec772c60ce96/dev/log/issues/31/pulls/32/SECURITY.md). body:
Fixes #27.

Equal reference gaps on a self-closed link now have exactly equal painted extents. The arrow correction uses each closed endpoint's tangent, removing the sudden jump between `0.07` and `0.08`, while retaining issue 25's common painted boundary for a lens referencing another link.

Automatic spacing preserves turns, reference gaps and middle cuts on fully or partially self-closed halves and optimizes open references. Shared URLs omit default turn rows and trailing inherited gap columns, accept every historical URL schema, and replace the address with the compact equivalent on arrival. A shared numeric component preserves intermediate text and inherited values, including native spinner clicks on empty inherited fields; all slider and number renderers support consistent decimal stepping and keyboard navigation.

### Reproduction and verification

Open `/network/?code=1111&rotation=-90&turns=0+0%2C-15+15&gaps=0.08+0.08+%7E+%7E%2C0.18+0.18+%7E+%7E`. Before the fix, source/target painted closed gaps measured **4.15 / 5.45** SVG units; after, **4.15 / 4.15**. Changing only the target from `0.07` to `0.08` now moves it by the expected **0.60**, rather than **1.90** units. The exact manual arrangement is a regression fixture.

- Geometry, full/partial closed-half solver, historical-schema, URL history and numeric editing regressions are included. Failed-before logs, raw numerical measurements and independent rasterized SVG checks are archived.
- `npm run check`, **737 unit tests** and production build pass. `npm run test:network:issue27` runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit alongside all existing browser suites in CI, with screenshots and JSON artifacts. Playwright MCP verifies actual native spinner Up/Down clicks, including inherited values.
- The [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/cdf0cd1c23ca741354fa076975984cb960176519/docs/case-studies/issue-27/README.md) inventories every requirement, reconstructs the timeline, audits all six historical URL schemas, explains the root causes and alternatives, and includes source data, prior-session logs and [validation evidence](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/cdf0cd1c23ca741354fa076975984cb960176519/docs/case-studies/issue-27/VALIDATION.md).

The solver remains an opt-in overlap heuristic: it preserves the closed link but can choose different open-link gaps/turns from the symmetric manual fixture. Its preview, applied result and shared reload are identical. No external dependency defect was identified in this issue.

Fixes #21.

Loading thousands of gallery cards kept a backdrop filter on every card, adding avoidable rendering pressure behind the fixed header. Offscreen cards, repositories and posts now disable their filters through one shared viewport observer; visible panels retain their selected skin. The redundant gallery Share icon is removed, leaving the full-card editor link.

The editor now starts with bend **0**, keeps full and partial self-loops balanced, and offers independent signed loop shaping. Displaced endpoint and middle markers follow arc length and the local tangent. Four optional gaps per link inherit global settings when blank, survive URL sharing/export and saved looks, and participate in the experimental overlap solver. Applying the solver preserves its preview exactly. Legacy gallery, rain and theory geometry remains covered by stored hashes.

The [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-23-729a1009db7c/docs/case-studies/issue-23/README.md) maps every requirement to its cause, implementation and evidence, including the complete audit of #21, archived reports/logs, research, alternatives and default-off diagnostics. The supplied Safari screenshots document the intermittent blink. Native display captures now verify bounded filter counts and visible blur in Chromium/Firefox on Linux and WebKit on macOS at the full reported load. The exact original Safari GPU failure remains unisolated; optional diagnostics are available for recurrence. A separately reproduced Firefox screenshot defect is reported upstream with a minimal example and workaround: [microsoft/playwright#43646](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43646).

### Reproduction and regression checks

On the original code, open `/network/?code=00000000` to see bent free links, or `/network/?code=11&startOffset=12&endOffset=12` to see displaced markers leave the loop. The old gallery also exposes two links per card and retains 4,131 filters after loading 4,131 cards. Failing geometry and DOM tests and production screenshots were captured before the fix.

- Geometry, curve, solver and DOM regressions cover neutral defaults, signed ranges, native curve placement, individual/inherited gaps, URL round-trips, exact applied previews, list-observer cleanup and a dense 24-link solver scaling regression.
- All four network browser suites run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, including real image downloads, source colors, supplied #21 URLs, history, mobile editing and actual composited header blur.
- All three engines pass the exact **4,131-card** load, repeated scrolling and actual display-pixel blur checks in all three skins, with **55–176 active card filters** and zero page errors. A separate audit passes all ten HTML entries across skins, themes, languages and desktop/mobile widths (**240 combinations**).
- **710 unit tests**, lint/format/line limits/secrets, dependency audit, production build and **120 CV PDFs** pass locally; detailed results are in [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-23-729a1009db7c/docs/case-studies/issue-23/VALIDATION.md).

Final head CI is green: [run 40276708061](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40276708061) at `cf1e6ec`, including all browser suites, 710 unit tests, builds and 120 PDFs. The complete source-validation evidence from [run 40275956453](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40275956453) at `0bc96b4` is archived in the case study; the final commit adds only that evidence. `main` is already included, and the working tree is clean.

### Visual comparison

![Before: nonzero default bend](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-23-729a1009db7c/docs/case-studies/issue-23/screenshots/chromium-before-free.png?raw=true)

title: Stabilize gallery blur and refine network editor geometry

body:
Fixes #21.

Clicking a network now opens the editor with symmetric loop defaults, cross-like starts and the colors shown at the source. Bend changes free-link curvature and self-loop width; free endpoints stay anchored. Gallery, theory and background-rain geometry retain their original construction.

- Match dark/light colors from gallery cards, share icons and theory examples; remove gallery hover underlines.
- Preserve independent angles, gaps, marker controls, placements, overlap reduction, exports and saved styles. Keep legacy tangent rotation selectable and recognize older explicit custom-color URLs.
- Verify both supplied URLs against their controls, then edit/share/reload to the same SVG. The screenshot values already parsed correctly; inherited defaults and bend construction caused the differences.

### Reproduction and verification

Open `/network/?code=1122` and `/network/?code=00000000`, vary Bend, and compare with gallery navigation. Equal endpoint angles/gaps give point-symmetric loops; free endpoints no longer rotate with Bend. Also hover a gallery card and open it in both themes.

Automated coverage: `src/links/geometry-21.test.js`, `src/pages/network-21.test.jsx`, and `npm run test:network:issue21`. Strict symmetry samples, all 4,181 small editor configurations, and 4,693 unchanged gallery/rain SVG hashes guard geometry and scope. Browser checks verify supplied settings, share/reload, dark/light navigation, hover, SVG export and mobile overflow.

Validation: 693 unit tests pass; repository checks and production build pass; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit pass the new and existing browser suites. CI also verifies CV PDFs and the Pages build artifact.

### Before / after

| ![Before: rotated free links](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-21-823573f25e74/docs/case-studies/issue-21/screenshots/chromium-before-default-00000000.png?raw=true) | ![After: anchored curves and cross starts](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-21-823573f25e74/docs/case-studies/issue-21/screenshots/chromium-after-default-00000000.png?raw=true) |

![Editor controls with the first supplied configuration](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-21-823573f25e74/docs/case-studies/issue-21/screenshots/chromium-after-supplied-1.png?raw=true)

[Complete case study, settings audit, requirement inventory, timeline, root causes, library research, raw logs/data and browser evidence](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/tree/issue-21-823573f25e74/docs/case-studies/issue-21). All causes were traced to this application; no external dependency defect required an upstream report.
title: Make editor geometry symmetric and preserve source colors
